docTitle: The Way — David | Walk the Life of David on a Map
metaDesc: From a shepherd boy in the fields of Bethlehem, through the Valley of Elah and the caves of the wilderness, to the king of Jerusalem. Walk 39 scenes of David's life on a Bible map, and hear the psalms he wrote in those places as songs.
mapAria: David's route on a map of Judah, Benjamin, Philistia and Gilead
introTag: The way of David, from the fields of Bethlehem to the palace in Jerusalem
introLead: Walk the map and follow the road of a shepherd boy who became a hunted man, then a king, who fell and rose again.
introF1: Follow the places, from Bethlehem through the Valley of Elah and the caves of the wilderness to Jerusalem
introF3: Hear the story read aloud, and listen to the psalms David wrote in those places as songs
landStep2: Read the story and the texts on the card, and press ▶ to hear it read aloud
landStep4: Gather the words of God and of David in the '{words}' tab, and revisit the scenes you have walked with '{quiz}'
wordsIntro: The words God spoke and the words David said along David's way, gathered in the order of the journey. Every saying is a fresh rendering of the original meaning in today's language.
odoTitle: Distance David has walked up to this scene (estimated road distance between places; steps at a 75 cm stride)
endLead: From the fields of Bethlehem to David's last song — thank you for walking with us.
blessing:
The Lord is my shepherd; I have all that I need.
He lets me lie down in green pastures and leads me beside quiet waters. (Ps 23:1–2)
May the one who called the boy in the fields call your name too, and may the one who was with him through the nights of flight guard your way.
psalmHead: The song sung in this place
psalmNote: A song from the Psalms journey, sung in Korean. The music and lyrics were made with AI and refined by people.
lessons:
God looks at the heart|The youngest shepherd boy, forgotten among his brothers, was called to be king. People look at outward appearance, but God looks at the heart. (1 Sam 16:7)
The way back after a fall|David sinned greatly, yet he did not hide; he bowed down before God. God does not despise a broken and repentant heart. (Ps 51:17)
A promise bigger than human failure|David's house was shaken to the end, yet God never took back his promise to establish his throne forever. (2 Sam 7:16)
gospelBridge: A thousand years later, the son of that promise was born in Bethlehem, the town of David. Like David the shepherd boy, he is a shepherd who knows his sheep. I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. (John 10:11)
invite:
If the story of God you met on this road has stayed with you, come and meet Jesus, who stands at the center of that story. Walk 'The Footsteps of Jesus' from the beginning, and visit a church near you. May you meet God in worship and in his word, be adopted as his child, and know the joy of calling God 'Father.' (Rom 8:15)
He is still standing at the door, waiting for you. (Rev 3:20)
seekerHead: For those who don’t yet know him
